method: Hand-written single-best-answer MCQs grounded only in the accepted open full text.

topic.topicDisplayName: ORAL Surveillance trial: cardiovascular safety of tofacitinib vs TNFi in RA
topic.coverageNote: The NEJM primary paper was not open on PMC. This open paper reports the ORAL Surveillance cardiovascular comparison and is used only for figures it states.

mcqs.question: What major-adverse-cardiovascular-event hazard ratio for tofacitinib versus TNF inhibitors does this report give from ORAL Surveillance?

options.E: The trial did not estimate a hazard ratio

mcqs.explanation: Primary findings indicated an increased MACE risk with tofacitinib versus TNF inhibitors, HR 1.33 (95% CI 0.91 to 1.94).

sourceRefs.excerpt: increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) with tofacitinib versus tumour necrosis factor inhibitors (TNFi) (hazard ratio=1.33; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.91 to 1.94).

mcqs.question: Why was non-inferiority of tofacitinib versus TNF inhibitors not met?

options.C: TNF inhibitors were not an allowed comparator

mcqs.explanation: Non-inferiority required the upper 95% confidence limit not to exceed 1.80; it was higher than 1.80, so the criterion was not met.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The non-inferiority criterion was not met (upper limit of 95% CI was >1.80).

mcqs.question: Which incidence rates of MACE per 100 patient-years are reported?

options.A: 0.98 with tofacitinib and 0.73 with TNF inhibitors
options.C: 5.0 with TNF inhibitors and 0.1 with tofacitinib
options.E: 10 with tofacitinib and 10 with TNF inhibitors

mcqs.correctAnswerText: 0.98 with tofacitinib and 0.73 with TNF inhibitors
mcqs.explanation: Adjudicated MACE incidence was 0.98 per 100 patient-years with tofacitinib and 0.73 with TNF inhibitors.

sourceRefs.excerpt: incidence rate (IR) of 0.98 per 100 patient-years, 95% CI 0.79 to 1.19, versus IR of 0.73 per 100 patient-years, 95% CI 0.52 to 1.01

mcqs.question: In which age group was the MACE increase with tofacitinib versus TNF inhibitors more pronounced?

options.A: Age 65 years or older, compared with under 65
options.C: The increase was confined to teenagers
options.D: Age had no relation to MACE

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Age 65 years or older, compared with under 65
mcqs.explanation: The increased MACE risk was more pronounced in patients aged 65 or older than in those under 65.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The increased risk of MACE with tofacitinib versus TNFi was more pronounced in patients aged ≥65 years than in patients aged <65 years.

mcqs.question: Besides MACE, which other risks does this report say were higher with tofacitinib than with TNF inhibitors in ORAL Surveillance?

options.A: Malignancies excluding non-melanoma skin cancer, and infections
options.B: Only injection-site reactions from TNF inhibitors
options.C: Neither malignancy nor infection differed in any report
options.E: Fractures were the sole additional endpoint and were lower

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Malignancies excluding non-melanoma skin cancer, and infections
mcqs.explanation: The report states that risk of malignancies excluding non-melanoma skin cancer, and of infections, was also higher with tofacitinib versus TNF inhibitors.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Risk of malignancies (excluding non-melanoma skin cancer) and infections was also higher with tofacitinib versus TNFi in ORAL Surveillance.
